android.desc:
Android port of the Frozen Bubble game.  Knock the bubbles down by forming clusters of three or more bubbles.

This version features 3 game modes: continuous Arcade, classic Puzzle, and versus play.

This game has no ads or in-app purchases.

Frozen Bubble for Android requires minimal permissions to support WiFi and Bluetooth network multiplayer.

quotes.text:
My personal experience: I submitted two personal projects http://kartofel.jfedor.org/ and https://market.android.com/details?id=org.jfedor.frozenbubble last year (in July I believe) and both were rejected (i.e., the committee said that Google would not release copyright).  However, recently (a month or two ago) I was told that the rules changed and now they were happy to release the copyright for both.  In the meantime I tried to get my employment agreement altered to state that my personal projects belong to me, not to Google, but I found there was absolutely no room for negotiation there (despite the fact that my manager, an eng director, supported this).  I was told by the legal department that the only person in the company who could approve such thing was Larry Page.

It is true that Google has a very easy process to open-source your projects.  One practical pain is that if you want to accept patches you have to get every contributor to sign Google's CLA.
quotes.story_title: Poll: Given the opportunity would you work at Google?
